gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price for any 25W wireless charger for the iPhone 17 other than Apple's, or says which ones include the adapter that 25W needs: ESR's Cyclone 25W pad costs $43.99 with no adapter, while Belkin's UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1 (WIZ040) costs $129.99 and includes a 45W USB-C power supply.
standout_why: I compared against the cited apple.com/iphone-17/specs page and the cited MagSafe Charger (1 m) pages. The specs page says 25W needs a '30W power adapter or higher (available separately)'. When fetched today, the MagSafe Charger pages showed no price and no 25W/iPhone 17 text; their footnote mentions only a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter for wired fast charging. None of the results names a third-party Qi2.2 charger, gives its price, or says whether an adapter is in the box. ChatGPT's answer shows no prices at all and tells the shopper to buy a 30W+ adapter without pricing it.
decides: This confirms that the page has to price the full 25W setup, not just the charger. A pad from ESR (or Apple's MagSafe Charger) still needs an adapter bought separately. Belkin WIZ040 ($129.99 with a 45W PSU included) is the one I checked today that works straight from the box. Anker Prime A25N1 ($149.99) costs the most and needs a 45W-or-higher adapter, more than Apple's 30W minimum. Its anker.com page does not say whether that adapter is included. The ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 ($109.99) undercuts Belkin by $20. Our page says it includes a 50W adapter, but I could not re-check that today.
